chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Affan narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Humayd, from Jabir ibn Abdillah al-Ansari who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, came out to us holding the hands of al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, and said: These two sons of mine — I raised them when they were young, and I prayed for them when they grew up, and I asked Allah the Exalted three things for them. He granted me two and denied me one. I asked Allah to make them pure, purified, and righteous — and He answered me in that. And I asked Allah to protect them, their offspring, and their followers from the Fire — and He granted me that. And I asked Allah to unite the community upon love for them, and He said: O Muhammad, indeed I have decreed a decree and ordained a destiny. A group from your community will fulfill your covenant regarding the Jews, the Christians, and the Zoroastrians, but they will betray your covenant regarding your children. And indeed I have obligated upon Myself that whoever does that, I shall not place him in the abode of My honor, nor house him in My Paradise, nor look upon him with the eye of My mercy until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.ذُرِّيَّة: offspring/progeny — the descendants of the two Imams
key_terms.ذِمَّة: covenant/pledge of protection — the Prophet's guarantee on behalf of his family
key_terms.شِيعَة: followers/partisans — referring to the devoted followers of Hasan and Husayn
key_terms.طَاهِرَيْنِ مُطَهَّرَيْنِ: pure and purified — echoing the Quranic verse of purification (33:33)

ai.seo_question: What three things did the Prophet Muhammad ask Allah for his grandsons Hasan and Husayn?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) relates his three supplications to Allah on behalf of his grandsons al-Hasan and al-Husayn (AS). Allah granted two — their spiritual purity and protection from Hell for them, their descendants, and their followers — but revealed that universal love for them would not be granted, as divine decree dictated that some would betray their covenant with the Prophet's family. This hadith, narrated by the companion Jabir al-Ansari, underscores the Shia theological position on the special status of the Prophet's grandchildren and the consequences for those who harm them.
